answer: A sybil tax makes fakes expensive: each agent pays a 50-credit fee that is burned, and a lantern registry publishes every payment. Before any reward, the ridge of verified payments is checked; no receipt means no earnings. An echo audit samples 10% of identities each epoch and burns clones. Making 1,000 fakes costs 50,000 credits, while each earns about 20, so the attack loses 30,000. An honest agent pays 50 credits once and keeps every reward.
